newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: OUB sees S$200 mln unit trusts by 2000.
newsitem.headline: OUB sees S$200 mln unit trusts by 2000.

text.p: Overseas Union Bank Ltd (OUB) President Peter Seah said on Friday the bank aimed to manage Singapore $200 million in unit trusts by the turn of the century.
Seah told Reuters in an interview that OUB planned a major push into the management of retail funds via unit trusts over the next few years.
He said the bank now managed unit trust funds of only around S$40 million, but hoped this would rise to around S$100 million by the end of the year.
"Over the next three years, we aim to at least double that," he said.
Seah said the Singapore unit trust market was fairly small in world terms, but was expected to grow rapidly as local investors became more and more sophisticated about investments.
Analysts say the total Singapore unit trust market is worth about S$2.9 billion. Seah said he expect that to grow to at least S$5.0 billion by 2000.
"As the public becomes more sophisticated in its use of surplus funds, use of unit trusts will grow," he said.
Seah was speaking after the announement of a new OUB unit trust to invest in health care, leisure, entertainment and wealth management.
